audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 is called hers but never says why in numbers; the entry reads as if Galio's tornado holds her off.
audit.why: Radiant Volley is 950 and Solar Snare 1000 against Winds of War's 825 — she out-ranges every tool Galio has, which is exactly why the opening belongs to her and why the lane only flips when he can close.
audit.corrected: Range numbers written into spikes[0], whys[0] and early. Matches the mirror at audits/top/mel__galio.json, which states the same 825 / 950 / 1000 gap from her side.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] says at 6 'she has no way to interrupt or follow the global', and whys[6] says 'your global R wins the map'.
audit.why: Two errors in one claim. Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140 at range 4000/4750/5500 onto an ALLY, not global. And Golden Eclipse has range 25000 and 'strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm REGARDLESS of their distance from her' — leaving the lane does not leave her ultimate.
audit.corrected: Both restated: your ult lands on an ally within 4000; hers finds you anywhere you carry Overwhelm.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings call Rebuttal her R and say it stuns: 'Her R, Rebuttal, reflects projectiles and stuns', 'Time her R, Rebuttal, to reflect and stun', 'you'll eat the reflect and stun'.
audit.why: Rebuttal is Mel's W, not her R — her R is Golden Eclipse. And Riot's description is 'a barrier around herself that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, prevents her from taking damage, and grants her movement speed'. There is no stun anywhere in it. The real cost of firing Q into it is that Winds of War comes back at you and the barrier eats the rest.
audit.corrected: Slot corrected to W, the stun removed, and the reflect made the reason to open with the dash instead of the tornado.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Track Solar Snare' appears eight times with no number attached to it or to Rebuttal.
audit.why: Solar Snare is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 from 1000 range, Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26, Golden Eclipse 120/100/80, and your Justice Punch is 11s at rank 1. Rebuttal at 38 seconds is the longest cooldown in the lane and the one worth baiting.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, loading and the mid/spikes text. Same figures the mirror used.

edits.before: Her R, Rebuttal, reflects projectiles and stuns — but your E is a dash and your W taunt is an aura, so neither gets reflected; the real trap is eating it with a mistimed Q. Bait it, then commit your full combo.
edits.after: Rebuttal is her W, not her R: it reflects projectiles, so Winds of War comes straight back at you. It does not stun. Your E is a dash and the taunt an aura, so open with those and hold Q until that 38-second barrier is spent.

edits.before: Time her R, Rebuttal, to reflect and stun if you fire Q into it, then kite back out of taunt range
edits.after: Pop Rebuttal (W, 38s at rank 1) when he fires Winds of War so the tornado reflects onto him

edits.before: You hold the 1v1 the whole way — she's a squishy ranged mage with no dash to escape a taunt-knockup that lands on top of her, so she can never duel you straight. Your job is to keep being a Galio: W-soak her R-window burst and the rest of the enemy AP with that amplified reduction, and use Hero's Entrance to swing fights across the map. Respect her passive execute when you're low, and don't throw Q into an active Rebuttal or you'll eat the reflect and stun — but in a teamfight you flag in, taunt her and her carries, and absorb the burst your shield is built for.
edits.after: You hold the 1v1 the whole way — she's a squishy ranged mage with no dash to escape a taunt-knockup that lands on top of her, so she can never duel you straight. Your job is to keep being a Galio: W-soak her burst and the rest of the enemy AP with that amplified reduction, and use Hero's Entrance, which lands on an ally up to 4000 units away, to swing fights. Respect her passive execute when you are low, and never fire Q into an active Rebuttal — it reflects the tornado back at you, though it does not stun. Distance is no escape from Golden Eclipse: it strikes every Overwhelm-marked enemy anywhere on the map.

edits.before: Hero's Entrance: flag onto her for a taunt-knockup all-in, or onto a sidelane to snowball — she has no way to interrupt or follow the global.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance: land on an ally for the knockup all-in or to snowball a sidelane — but Golden Eclipse reaches you at any distance.

edits.before: This is your lane. You out-trade her any time you can land E-knockup into the W-release taunt — she has no mobility to dodge the dash, and her R (Rebuttal) only punishes you if you fire a projectile like Q into it. So don't open with Q: E in first, W-taunt, and let your Colossal Smash empowered auto plus a point-blank Q delete her while she's locked. At 6, Hero's Entrance is your real spike — flag onto her for the all-in or onto a sidelane to snowball, because she can't 1v1 a Galio who soaks her magic and she has no way to stop the global.
edits.after: This is your lane. You out-trade her any time you land E-knockup into the W-release taunt — she has no dash to dodge it, and Justice Punch only stops on a champion, so her minions do not shield her. Her Rebuttal (W, 38s at rank 1) reflects projectiles, so do not open with Q: E in first, taunt, then let the Colossal Smash empowered auto and a point-blank Q delete her while she is locked. At 6, Hero's Entrance lands on an ally 4000 units away — but Golden Eclipse still finds you anywhere if you carry Overwhelm stacks.

edits.before: Your first item and shorter cooldowns out-pace her — open with E (a dash, not a reflectable projectile), W-taunt, then empowered auto plus point-blank Q to burst her down.
edits.after: Your first item and shorter cooldowns out-pace her — open with E, a dash rather than a reflectable projectile, then the taunt, the empowered auto and a point-blank Q.

edits.before: You keep the duel all game: she can't 1v1 through your amplified magic soak and taunt-knockup, and your global R wins the map even as she scales.
edits.after: You keep the duel all game, but Golden Eclipse hits Overwhelm-marked targets at any range — leaving the lane does not leave her ultimate.

edits.before: Level 1 is hers — you have only one ability and no engage, so eat the Q poke at the tornado's edge and just last-hit; don't walk up to contest while she pokes free. The lane flips the moment you hit 3. Once Q-W-E are up, her all-AP poke is exactly what Shield of Durand wants: start the W-channel into her Q windblasts, where the heavily magic-amplified damage reduction blunts the chunk, then E through her for the knockup and pop the release taunt. Her whole kit is ranged AP with no dash to peel your E, so every time she steps up to poke she's inside taunt range.
edits.after: Level 1 is hers — you have only one ability and no engage, and she out-ranges you: Radiant Volley reaches 950 and Solar Snare 1000 against your 825. Eat the poke at the tornado's edge and last-hit. The lane flips the moment you hit 3. Once Q-W-E are up, her all-AP poke is exactly what Shield of Durand wants: start the W-channel into her Q, where the heavily magic-amplified reduction blunts the chunk, then E through her for the knockup and pop the release taunt. She has no dash to peel it, so every step-up she makes puts her inside taunt range.

edits.before: Mel's window: you have one ability and no engage, so she chips you with Q overwhelm and free auto poke while you can only last-hit at the tornado's edge.
edits.after: Mel's window: you have one ability and no engage, and she out-ranges you — Radiant Volley 950 and Solar Snare 1000 against your 825. Last-hit at the edge.

edits.before: Level 1 you have one ability and no engage while Mel pokes with Q and free autos and stacks her passive safely — she owns the opening before your kit comes online.
edits.after: Level 1 you have one ability and no engage while Mel pokes from 950 to your 825 and stacks Overwhelm safely — she owns the opening before your kit is online.

edits.before: - Mel Solar Snare: matchup-defining — Her root / slow zone — sets up her combo. Dodge it. Track it before every punch. - Your W: the trade-flipper — never burn it early. - Your R: a map-wide win condition — spend it on allies' fights.
edits.after: - Solar Snare: 11s at rank 1, 9s maxed, from 1000 — her root, and the thing that stops your dash. - Rebuttal: 38s at rank 1, and it reflects Winds of War, so never open with Q. - Golden Eclipse: 120s, and it reaches you anywhere. - Your E: 11s.

edits.after: Rebuttal reflects your Winds of War — open with the dash, not the tornado. Solar Snare roots your punch out of the air.

edits.after: - Galio vs Mel - Never open with Q: Rebuttal reflects it. - Open with the E dash, taunt on release. - Solar Snare 11s roots your punch. - Golden Eclipse reaches anywhere.

edits.after: Mel wins by rooting your punch with Solar Snare, reflecting your Q, and executing you late.

notes: Headline error: three strings call Rebuttal Mel's R and say it STUNS. Rebuttal is her W — her R is Golden Eclipse — and Riot's description is reflect, damage immunity and move speed, with no stun at all. A Galio player reading this would both fear a stun that does not exist and never learn that her actual ultimate ignores distance. Second: spikes[2] told the player she 'has no way to interrupt or follow the global' at 6, when Golden Eclipse has range 25000 and strikes every Overwhelm-marked enemy regardless of distance — the exact opposite of the advice. Mirror-aligned with audits/top/mel__galio.json on the 825/950/1000 range gap, Justice Punch's 11s and backward-hop tell, and Rebuttal's 38s. Per that mirror's note I did NOT claim Hero's Entrance interrupts Golden Eclipse; the kit gives Golden Eclipse no channel flag and there is no support either way.
